'''Iwaki no Kuni no Miyatsuko''' (石城国造, also read as Iwaki Kokuzō) was the {{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|en|Kuni no miyatsuko|qid=Q2483673|lt=Kuni no Miyatsuko}} who governed the region known as {{ill|Iwaki Province (718)|en|Iwaki Province (718)|qid=Q1192809|lt=Iwaki Province}} (later part of southern {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|qid=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}} under the Ritsuryō system).

== Overview ==

=== Ancestry ===
* According to the ''{{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|qid=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kuji Hongi}}'' (Chronicle of Former Kings), the lineage begins with '''{{ill|Tatekoromikoto|ja|建許呂命}}''', who was appointed as Kuni no Miyatsuko during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ar|الإمبراطور سيمو|arz|الامبراطور سيمو|azb|سیمو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Seimu|cs|Seimu|de|Seimu|es|Seimu Tennō|fa|امپراتور سیمو|fi|Seimu|fr|Seimu|hr|Seimu|hu|Szeimu japán császár|id|Kaisar Seimu|it|Seimu|ja|成務天皇|ka|სეიმუ|ko|세이무 천황|nl|Seimu|pl|Seimu|pt|Seimu|ru|Император Сэйму|sh|Car Seimu|simple|Emperor Seimu|sl|Cesar Sejmu|sv|Seimu|th|จักรพรรดิเซมุ|tl|Emperador Seimu|tr|Seimu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Сейму|uz|Imperator Seimu|vi|Thiên hoàng Seimu|yo|Emperor Seimu|zh|成務天皇|zh_min_nan|Seimu Thian-hông|zh_yue|成務天皇|qid=Q316672|lt=Emperor Seimu}}.
* In the fragment of the ''{{ill|Fudoki|en|Fudoki|qid=Q1194534|lt=Fudoki}}'' of Mutsu Province, the name of '''Iwaki-hiko''' (磐城彦) appears as a Kuni no Miyatsuko.

=== Clan ===
The ruling clan was the '''{{ill|Iwaki clan|de|Iwaki (Klan)|ja|岩城氏|ru|Иваки (род)|zh|岩城氏|qid=Q11474314|lt=Iwaki clan}}''' (石城氏, Iwaki-uji), bearing the hereditary title ({{ill|Kabane|en|Kabane|qid=Q1664099|lt=Kabane}}) of '''Ason''' (直).
* The ''Kuni no Miyatsuko Honki'' states that ''Tatekoromikoto'', a descendant of {{ill|Amatsuhikone|ja|天津彦根命}}, was the ancestor of the Iwaki no Kuni no Miyatsuko.
* The ''{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}'' records that {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Kamuyamato Iwarebiko}}’s son, {{ill|Kamuyaimimi|fr|Kamuyaimimi|ja|神八井耳命|ko|카무야이미미노미코토|simple|Kamuyaimimi|zh|神八井耳命|qid=Q11588756|lt=Kamiyai-mimi no Mikoto}}, was the ancestor of the Ōomi, the Dōoku Iwaki no Kuni no Miyatsuko, among others.

== Headquarters ==

=== Territory ===
The Kuni no Miyatsuko governed the region known as '''Iwaki Province''' (石城国), corresponding to the later '''{{ill|Iwaki District, Mutsu Province|ja|石城郡|qid=Q11585428}}''' in {{ill|Mutsu Province|en|Mutsu Province|qid=Q907389|lt=Mutsu Province}}. This roughly equates to the modern {{ill|Hamadōri|id|Hamadōri|it|Hamadōri|ja|浜通り|ko|하마도리|ru|Хамадори|zh|濱通|qid=Q845466|lt=Hamadōri region}} in {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|en|Fukushima Prefecture|qid=Q71707|lt=Fukushima Prefecture}}, particularly from the northern part of {{ill|Iwaki, Fukushima|en|Iwaki, Fukushima|qid=Q274384|lt=Iwaki, Fukushima}} to {{ill|Ōkuma, Fukushima|arz|اوكوما|bn|ওকুমা, ফুকুশিমা|ceb|Ōkuma Machi|de|Ōkuma (Fukushima)|el|Όκουμα|es|Ōkuma (Fukushima)|et|Ōkuma|fa|اوکوما، فوکوشیما|fr|Ōkuma|hu|Ókuma|id|Ōkuma, Fukushima|it|Ōkuma|ja|大熊町|jv|Ōkuma, Fukushima|ko|오쿠마정|ms|Ōkuma, Fukushima|my|အိုးခုမမြို့၊ ဖူကူရှီးမား|nl|Ōkuma|pl|Ōkuma|pt|Ōkuma|ru|Окума|sco|Ōkuma, Fukushima|simple|Ōkuma, Fukushima|sr|Окума|th|โอกูมะ|tl|Ōkuma, Fukushima|tr|Ōkuma|uk|Окума|ur|اوکوما، فوکوشیما|uz|Ōkuma (Fukushima)|vi|Ōkuma, Fukushima|zh|大熊町|zh_yue|大熊町|qid=Q385311|lt=Ōkuma, Fukushima}}.

By the mid-7th century, the region merged with the domains of {{ill|Michi no Oku Kikuta no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|道奥菊多国造|qid=Q11641674}} (to the south) and {{ill|Taka no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|高国造|qid=Q11668988}} to form {{ill|Taga Province|ja|多珂国}}. The northern boundary of the Iwaki domain was marked by ''Kuruma Village'' (苦麻の村) in what is now Ōkuma, as mentioned in the ''{{ill|Hitachi Fudoki|ja|常陸国風土記}}''.

== Ancestral Deities ==

* '''{{ill|Ōkunitama Shrine|en|Ōkunitama Shrine|qid=Q611678|lt=Ōkunitama Shrine (Iwaki)}}'''  
Located in the historical {{ill|Kunitama district|ja|国魂郷}} of Iwaki District, at 26 Miyamae, Sugawara, {{ill|Iwaki, Fukushima|en|Iwaki, Fukushima|qid=Q274384|lt=Iwaki, Fukushima}}, Fukushima Prefecture.

=== Related Shrines ===
* '''{{ill|Iwaki Kokuzō Shrine|ja|磐城国造神社}}'''  
Situated in {{ill|Onahama, Iwaki|ja|小名浜}}, enshrining {{ill|Tatekoromikoto|ja|建許呂命}}.

=== Tomb ===
* '''{{ill|Kabutozuka Kofun (Iwaki)|ja|甲塚古墳}}'''  
A round Kofun (円墳), 8 meters high with a diameter of 37 meters, believed to be the tomb of Tatekoromikoto, located 200 meters east of Ōkunitama Shrine. It is a designated National Historic Site.

== Descendants ==

* '''Ishikawa no Hyoujō Shikoseki'''  
According to the ''Hitachi Fudoki,'' in 653 (9th year of {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|en|Emperor Kōtoku|qid=Q317980|lt=Emperor Kōtoku}}), Shikoseki petitioned the Eastern Governor with Ishikawa no Miyabe of Taga Province for administrative division.

* '''Ō Iwaki no Omi Yamagishi'''  
In 769 (3rd year of {{ill|Jingo-keiun|en|Jingo-keiun|qid=Q1373049|lt=Jingō-keiun}}), he held the court Rank of Senior Sixth Rank, Upper Grade (外正六位上) and changed his family name from Takebe (丈部) to Ō Iwaki no Omi.

* '''Ō Iwaki no Omi Oishiki'''  
Granted the Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade (外従五位下) in 782 (2nd year of {{ill|Ten'ō|ja|天応 (日本)}}{{citation needed|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'ō}}).

* '''Iwaki no Omi Chisada'''  
Mentioned in lacquered documents from {{ill|Taga Castle|en|Taga Castle|qid=Q870867|lt=Tagajō}} dated to 780 (11th year of {{ill|Hōki|en|Hōki|qid=Q18520676|lt=Hōki}}).<ref name="Hirakawa">{{Cite journal|author=Minami Hirakawa|title=Short Essay on Satotoji: From the Second Wooden Tablet of the Aratame Site in Iwaki|journal=Bulletin of the National Museum of Japanese History|date=1996-02|doi=10.15024/00000757}}</ref>

* '''Iwaki no Omi Tōsei'''  
Promoted to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade (外従五位下) in 826 (3rd year of {{ill|Tenchō|de|Tenchō|es|Tenchō|fa|تنچو|fr|Ère Tenchō|ia|Tencho|id|Tenchō|ja|天長|ko|덴초|ru|Тэнтё|simple|Tenchō|sr|Тенчо|th|เท็นโจ|tr|Tenchō|uk|Тентьо|zh|天長 (日本)|zh_yue|天長 (年號)|qid=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō}}).

* '''Iwaki no Omi Yūkō''', '''Iwaki no Omi Sadamichi''', '''Iwaki no Omi Tomonari''', '''Iwaki no Omi Akiō'''  
According to the ''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1041301|lt=Shoku Nihon Kōki}}'', in 840 (11th year of {{ill|Jōwa|en|Jōwa|qid=Q3577279|lt=Jōwa}}), Yūkō, the Governor of Iwaki District, was granted the surname ''Abe Iwaki no Omi.''

* '''{{ill|Iwaki clan|de|Iwaki (Klan)|ja|岩城氏|ru|Иваки (род)|zh|岩城氏|qid=Q11474314|lt=Iwaki clan}} / {{ill|Iwaki clan|ja|磐城氏|lt=Iwaki clan}}'''  
Also known as the ''Kunitama clan,'' serving as chief priests of Ōkunitama Shrine.
